name: Park Hyatt Canberra
positioning: Historic Art Deco-style hotel beside Canberra's National Triangle, officially named Hyatt Hotel Canberra - A Park Hyatt Hotel, with heritage gardens and courtyards
best_for: Travelers visiting Canberra's national museums, galleries and Parliament House
Guests who enjoy a traditional afternoon tea in a heritage setting

facts.text: The hotel sits beside the National Triangle in Canberra.
Rooms have garden or courtyard views and large marble bathrooms.
Some rooms are located in the hotel's Heritage section.
The Presidential Suite's balconies overlook the gardens and Lake Burley Griffin.
The Promenade Cafe is furnished to complement the hotel's Art Deco style.
Speaker's Corner Bar has an open fire in winter and verandas in summer.
Guests can relax with bar snacks and drinks in the hotel's heritage gardens.
The Clubhouse offers a gym, personal trainers, an indoor pool, a sauna, fitness classes and bike hire.
Nearby sights include the National Museum of Australia, the National Portrait Gallery and Parliament House.
EV charging in the hotel car park is free for guests.
Canberra Airport is 9 kilometers from the hotel.

highlights.text: For more than a century the hotel has hosted heads of state, diplomats and captains of industry.
The Tea Lounge is in the hotel's heritage-listed residence and serves a traditional afternoon tea.
The Presidential Suite has a baby grand piano.
The hotel has historic Rose and Lavender Courtyards.
All rooms have large soak tubs and Le Labo amenities.

considerations.text: A 10% surcharge applies at the restaurants on Sundays and 15% on public holidays.
High tea at The Tea Lounge requires reservations.
WhataHotel notes the government-focused location may feel quiet on weekends.
